Explore Google Cloud from your AI conversation.

Connect your AI client to Google Cloud inventory and monitoring without giving it a service account key. GateRook searches Cloud Asset Inventory, reads current state from supported service APIs and queries Cloud Monitoring. Projects, folders and organizations stay explicit in the connection and its policy.

The route

Your AI requests a tool. GateRook checks the endpoint policy, resolves credentials locally, and calls the configured service.

Put context to work

What you can do with Google Cloud and AI

Investigate Cloud Run behavior

Find a service, inspect its current configuration and query its request or latency metrics. Give AI concrete resource state and a bounded monitoring interval to work with.

Map a project before debugging

Search inventory across the allowed scope for Compute Engine, Cloud SQL, GKE and other resource types, then inspect the specific resources involved in the incident.

Connect cloud and cluster evidence

Use the GCP connector to inspect a GKE cluster and the Kubernetes connector to read workload state within it. Each connection keeps its own permissions and limits.

From service to MCP

How to connect Google Cloud

GateRook must be running on a computer that can reach your service. Open Connections, choose Add connection, and select GCP. Give the connection a name and environment.

New to GateRook? Start with the full setup guide.
  1. 01

    Prepare Google credentials

    For ADC, run gcloud auth application-default login on the computer running GateRook. Alternatively, prepare a service account key for the protected connection field. Use an identity with the required inventory, monitoring and service read permissions.

  2. 02

    Set the project scope

    Add a GCP connection named stage-gcp in the stage environment. Enter projects/acme-stage, choose the credential source and optionally configure service account impersonation.

  3. 03

    Check monitoring and live reads

    Set metrics projects when needed, keep live reads enabled for current resource state, and run Test connection. Check the environment Cloud policy before saving so only intended services and resources are visible.

  4. 04

    Choose the endpoint and tool modes

    Add the tested connection to an endpoint. In Tools & policies, enable only the tools needed for the task. Start with Read only where supported; use Approval for any selected mutation and leave other tools Off. A connection alone does not grant an AI client access.

  5. 05

    Connect your AI and verify the first call

    In Clients, choose your AI app and endpoint, review the connection details, and connect. Try this guide’s example in Playground before asking your AI. Open Activity to inspect the tool, target, decision and returned result. The getting started guide covers this shared flow.

Connection settings

Configure Google Cloud in GateRook

These are example values for the connection form. Enter credentials into GateRook’s secret fields, not into an AI prompt. Requirements and alternatives are noted per field.

Google Cloud connection configuration
SettingExampleHow to use it
Projects, folders or organizationsprojects/acme-stageAdd the scopes this connection may search. Each scope must be accessible to the configured identity.
Credentials sourceadcUse Application Default Credentials on this computer, or choose serviceAccountKey and store its JSON in the protected field.
Impersonategw-reader@acme-stage.iam.gserviceaccount.comOptional service account impersonation. Your source identity must be allowed to impersonate this account.
Metrics projectsacme-stageDefaults to the project scopes. Folder and organization scopes need explicit projects for monitoring queries.
Read current state from service APIstrueWhen inspecting a supported resource by full name, read the service API instead of relying only on the inventory snapshot.

Know what you expose

Google Cloud tools and access boundaries

The connector determines what is possible. Endpoint modes and connection policies determine what a particular AI client may use.

Available tools and access behavior
ToolPurposeAccess behavior
gcp_describeSearch Cloud Asset Inventory by scope, asset type and query. Pass a returned full resource name to inspect its state, using a live service API when supported.Read only
gcp_metricsQuery Cloud Monitoring time series with filters, alignment and reduction; discover recently active metric types or inspect alerts.Read only

Before you enable access

  • The Google Cloud connector is read-only. It does not deploy services, modify IAM, restart instances or delete resources.
  • Cloud Asset search results can lag behind the service. Supported live reads cover Compute Engine, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, GKE, Pub/Sub, Storage bucket metadata, Cloud Functions and Memorystore.
  • A live read returns resource metadata, not arbitrary object contents or secret payloads. Unsupported live routes fall back to inventory data.
  • The source identity, impersonation permissions, enabled service APIs and gateway Cloud policy all affect which requests succeed.

GateRook stores local connection secrets encrypted and resolves them for connectors. Allowed tool results are returned to your AI client and may be processed by its provider. Scope the data you expose as well as the actions you allow.

Practical answers

Google Cloud connection questions

Use Test connection to isolate service access problems. Use Playground and Activity to inspect endpoint permissions and tool calls.

Can I use my existing gcloud login?

Use Application Default Credentials, which are separate from a normal gcloud CLI login. The connection form names gcloud auth application-default login as the setup command for ADC.

Are inventory results always current?

No. Cloud Asset Inventory can be minutes behind. Inspect a resource by the full name returned by search to use a live service read where supported, and check whether the response source is live or inventory.

Can I use a folder or organization scope?

Yes, when the configured identity can read that scope. Configure individual metrics projects as well if you want Cloud Monitoring queries; folder and organization scopes do not automatically select monitoring projects.
